html:
Premchand was the pen name of Dhanpat Rai Srivastava, the greatest writer of fiction in Hindi and Urdu. He was the first to make the village poor of north India the centre of serious novels and stories.

He was born in 1880 in a village near Varanasi, the son of a postal clerk, and lost both parents young. He worked as a schoolteacher and school inspector for twenty years.

He began in Urdu. In 1909 his book of patriotic stories was banned and the copies burnt by the district officer, who warned him to write no more. He took the name Premchand to carry on, and moved over time to Hindi, which had more readers. In 1921 he heard Gandhi speak and resigned his government post.

He wrote about a dozen novels and some 300 short stories. His subjects were debt, the landlord and moneylender, caste, dowry and the lot of widows. Godaan, "The Gift of a Cow", published in 1936, follows a farmer who wants only to own a cow and dies in debt. In the story "Kafan" a father and son drink away the money begged for a dead woman's shroud. "The Chess Players" was filmed by Satyajit Ray.

He died poor in 1936, months after chairing the first meeting of India's Progressive Writers' Association.
sum: Premchand was the pen name of Dhanpat Rai Srivastava, the greatest writer of fiction in Hindi and Urdu. He was the first to make the village poor of north India the centre of serious novels and stories.
